title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth relative curve. P_{X/S} is the sheaf of local étale coordinates, i.e. étale maps to P^1_S. H = PGL_{2,S} acts on P_{X/S} by Möbius transformations. Conn_{X/S} is the sheaf of projective connections, a torsor under ω^{⊗2}_{X/S}. The map c^X : P_{X/S} → Conn_{X/S} satisfies c^X(s) − c^X(t) = G(t,s).

On the previous page Grothendieck writes G(t,s) with divided derivatives D^{(n)} = (1/n!) d^n/dt^n, which make sense in any characteristic. He gets G = 12·G_0 with G_0(t,s) = −D^{(3)}s/D^{(1)}s + (D^{(2)}s/D^{(1)}s)^2. Up to normalisation G_0 is the Schwarzian: {s,t} = −6 G_0 and G = −2{s,t}. This gives an integral refinement: a finer torsor Conn_{0,X/S} under ω^{⊗2}, with c_0^X : P → Conn_0 and c_0^X(s) − c_0^X(t) = G_0(t,s). Conn_{X/S} is obtained from it by pushing out along 12·id : ω^{⊗2} → ω^{⊗2}.

This page, first part. The earlier statements extend from (Conn, G, c^X) to (Conn_0, G_0, c_0^X). This includes the map H\P_{X/S} → Conn_0, which in characteristic 0 is injective but not surjective. The extension is compatible with the canonical morphism Conn_0 → Conn lying over 12·id on the operator groups. Hence the notation c_0^X = (1/12) c^X.

This page, characteristic p. Let O'_X be the subsheaf of functions killed by D^{(1)}, D^{(2)}, D^{(3)}. The margin says O' = O^{(p)} (p-th powers) when p ≠ 2,3, and a higher Frobenius power otherwise. The hope, marked 'OK' in the margin, is that the map H_{X^{(p/S)}} \ P_{X/S} → Conn_{0,X/S} is injective. In words: PGL_2 with coefficients in p-th powers (functions on the Frobenius twist) leaves the Schwarzian invariant, and should be the full fibre of c_0.

Local Proposition. Hypotheses: A of characteristic p > 3, local or more generally with ₂Pic(A) = 0; B = A[T]/(T^p − α), the local model of a curve over its Frobenius twist; t the class of T. Let s = Σ_{i<p} a_i t^i with D^{(1)}s a unit and c_0(s) = 0, i.e. (D^{(2)}s)^2 = D^{(1)}s · D^{(3)}s. Conclusion: s = (at+b)/(ct+d) with a, b, c, d ∈ A and ad − bc = 1, unique up to a scalar unit.

Proof (next page).
- By flat extension adjoin α^{1/p} and translate t, so that α ∈ tB and t is t-adically small.
- Then D^{(1)}s ≡ a_1 mod t, so a_1 is a unit. Normalise s ↦ a_1^{-1}(s − a_0), then s ↦ s/(1 + a_2 s), to reach s ≡ t mod t^3.
- If s = t + a t^d + (higher terms) with 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1, compare modulo t^{d−2}. This gives binom(d,3)·a = 0.
- binom(d,3) is invertible since p > 3 and d < p, so a = 0. Induction gives s = t.

Role. This is the key local step for a characteristic-p analogue of 'integrability by algebraic functions': the fibres of the Schwarzian map are exactly PGL_2(O^p)-orbits. In modern terms this is the local content of Frobenius-projective structures and dormant PGL_2-opers.
errors: Margin on O': D^{(1)}, D^{(2)}, D^{(3)} all kill f^{p^2} in characteristic 2 and 3, but not f^p. Indeed D^{(2)}(u^2) = (D^{(1)}u)^2 for p=2 and D^{(3)}(u^3) = (D^{(1)}u)^3 for p=3. So the correct sheaf for p=2,3 is O^{(p^2)}. If the margin reads p^3, it overshoots.
'Isomorphisme can. Conn_0 → Conn' and 'iso 12 id' are isomorphisms only when 12 is invertible on S; in general they are morphisms (a push-out of torsors).

Normalising to ad − bc = 1 needs a square root of the unit det; otherwise the matrix is only determined in PGL_2(A). This is presumably why the hypothesis 'local, or ₂Pic(A) = 0' appears. The statement is cleaner as an element of PGL_2(A).

The Proposition as stated (α arbitrary, A not complete) needs the reduction on the next page: fpqc extension adjoining α^{1/p}, plus a check that the PGL_2 element descends. This is plausible by uniqueness but not written out.
The proof needs p > 3. For p = 2,3 the statement must be modified (coefficients in O^{p^2}); the notes only say p ≠ 2,3 'pour fixer les idées'.

ideas.what: Integral (divided-power) Schwarzian G_0 = −D^{(3)}s/D^{(1)}s + (D^{(2)}s/D^{(1)}s)^2 and the refined torsor Conn_0 under ω^{⊗2} from which projective connections arise by push-out along 12·id
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative over Z / integral model of the torsor of projective structures (PGL_2-opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Schwarzian (Schwarz, Kummer); integral and characteristic-p versions appear implicitly in Ihara (1974) and Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory)

ideas.what: Invariance of the Schwarzian under Möbius transformations with coefficients in p-th powers (functions on X^{(p/S)}), and the expectation that H_{X^{(p)}}\P_{X/S} → Conn_0 is injective
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius-projective structures; kernel of the Schwarzian map in characteristic p; dormant PGL_2-opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (Schwarzian equations, 1974); S. Mochizuki (1990s); Y. Hoshi (Frobenius-projective structures)

ideas.what: Local proposition: over B = A[t]/(t^p − α) with p > 3, vanishing of G_0(t,s) implies s is a Möbius transform of t with coefficients in A, proved by t-adic normalisation and invertibility of binom(d,3) for 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic-p rigidity lemma for solutions of the Schwarzian equation

missed.claim: In characteristic p > 3, Grothendieck proves locally that the fibres of the (integral) Schwarzian map are exactly PGL_2(O^{p})-orbits: c_0(s) = 0 implies s = (at+b)/(ct+d) with coefficients in A = O_{X^{(p)}}. This sets up an injective map H_{X^{(p/S)}}\P_{X/S} → Conn_{0,X/S}, the characteristic-p analogue of 'connections integrable by algebraic functions'. It is essentially the local foundation of Frobenius-projective structures, apparently around 1972, before Ihara's 1974 Schwarzian paper and long before Mochizuki and Hoshi.
missed.quote: Supposons c_0(s)=0 ... Alors ∃ a,b,c,d ∈ A ... avec ad−bc=1, tels que s = (at+b)/(ct+d)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the characteristic-p Schwarzian / dormant-oper circle of ideas, and a direct link between Grothendieck's work on the Cartier operator and Gauss-Manin connection and p-adic Teichmüller theory.

missed.claim: The integral refinement Conn_0 (with Conn = 12·Conn_0) gives a uniform treatment over Spec Z, including characteristic 2 and 3. There, by the previous page, all c^X(t) coincide, giving a canonical projective connection, and the correct invariance sheaf is O^{p^2}. This small-characteristic picture for projective structures and opers is little developed in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Opers and dormant opers in characteristic 2 and 3, and integral models of moduli of projective structures, are areas where a canonical integral normalisation of the Schwarzian is useful.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, finished characteristic-p rigidity lemma for the Schwarzian is embedded in Grothendieck's construction of an integral torsor of projective connections, apparently early (c. 1972). The underlying ideas are known today (Ihara, Mochizuki, Hoshi) and the lemma itself is routine, so this is a notable unpublished detail and possible priority point rather than an unknown result.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'H^1 P_{X/S}' should read 'H\P_{X/S}': the quotient of P_{X/S} by the group sheaf H = PGL_2, not a cohomology group.

First lines: likely '... et de H\P_{X/S} → Conn_{X/S} s'étendent à G_0(t,s) et à H\P_{X/S} → Conn_{0,X/S}, les premières se déduisant du second de façon évidente, compte tenu de l'homomorphisme can. Conn_0 → Conn ...'.
'compatible avec l'iso' is probably 'compatible avec l'homomorphisme ω^{⊗2} --12 id--> ω^{⊗2}'.
'On va espérer' is probably 'On va vérifier', matching the 'OK' in the margin.
Proposition hypothesis: likely 'A anneau de car p>0 local (plus généralement, avec ₂Pic(A)=0)'.
Margin: the exponent for p = 2,3 should mathematically be O^{(p^2)}; check the image reading 'p^3'.
The arrow H_{X^{(p/S)}}\P_{X/S} → Conn_{0,X/S} is a one-way map claimed injective, not a bijection '↔'.
